quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway?

options.text: 65 mph
75 mph
80 mph
Any of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Any of the above
questions.explanation: Rural interstate highways can have speed limits of 65, 70, 75, or 80 mph. Speed limits vary by location. Always follow the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When can a driver under 18 have passengers in their car?

options.text: When they get their license
When they have had their license for six months
When they turn 17
When driving to or from school

questions.correctAnswerText: When they have had their license for six months
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 cannot have passengers (except family members) until they have had their license for six months. There are exceptions for farm work and emergencies.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution
Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed
Cross the tracks at your own risk
Find another way across the tracks

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast, you must not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or signals are not working.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn
Wave your arms
Use your emergency lights
Flash your headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another car is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop
Slam on your brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you must use extra force to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicycle is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder
Go between them
Let the car pass, then pass the bicycle
Pass the bicycle quickly

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicycle
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicycle. Do not try to fit between both at the same time.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes
Drive to the right side of the road and stop
Signal the emergency vehicle to pass
Merge to the right lane and keep driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, clear it first, then stop on the right.

questions.question: At night, dim your lights when you are within ____ of the vehicle ahead.

options.text: 100 feet
200 feet
300 feet
500 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: At night, switch your headlights to low beam when you are within 300 feet of another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right
Hiking trails ahead and to the right
Hotel ahead and to the right
Hospital ahead and to the right

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: The faster your vehicle is going, the longer it takes to stop when other drivers do something unexpected.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Higher speed means longer stopping distance. You need more time to react and stop when other drivers make unexpected moves.

questions.question: Which recommendation does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your pupils shrink. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to normal light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.
If your vehicle is not touching the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder unless you have an emergency.

questions.question: Your accelerator gets stuck while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and push the brake pedal firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and push the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Quickly shift into neutral and push the brake pedal firmly. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
It only works when there is also a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly and carefully.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, slow down and drive carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead—they work better in fog.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means drivers should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge into their lane.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge in.

questions.question: You can pass on a two-lane road when there is a solid yellow line on your side of the center line.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a busy intersection. You cannot see around the other cars. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly once the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for a driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start turning left until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and safe.

questions.question: What will help a person recover from drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time allows alcohol to leave your body.

questions.question: When you see an accident, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Only stop if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop just to look at an accident, fire, or other disaster.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. You should:

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly after a blowout. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Slow down by taking your foot off the gas. When you are moving slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull to a safe spot.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should slow to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. The new speed limit shown on the sign starts right at that sign.
